name: CrossFit Mayhem
who: Rich Froning's home box and training compound, anchor of the Mayhem Nation programming and apparel brand.
why: Base for a four-time individual and multiple-time team CrossFit Games champion; drives one of the sport's largest media operations.

name: PRVN Fitness
who: Garage-style training facility built by coach Shane Orr for his wife Tia-Clair Toomey-Orr's programming brand.
why: Home base of the most decorated woman in CrossFit Games history, now a widely followed methodology and gear brand.

name: CrossFit Invictus
who: Longstanding San Diego box and one of the sport's most influential coaching-education and programming brands.
why: Its methodology and seminars shaped how competitive CrossFit is coached worldwide since the mid-2000s.

name: CompTrain (formerly CrossFit New England)
who: Ben Bergeron's strength-and-conditioning gym, rebuilt from the de-affiliated CrossFit New England.
why: Produced Mat Fraser and Katrin Davidsdottir; its whiteboard-and-mindset culture became a template copied across the sport.
warning: De-affiliated from CrossFit HQ and rebranded CompTrain; no longer an official CrossFit affiliate but still the same physical gym and program lineage.

name: Training Think Tank
who: Atlanta-area box built around a coaching staff of CrossFit Games veterans, led by nine-time Games athlete Travis Mayer.
why: One of the deeper competitive coaching benches outside the traditional CrossFit power centers, with a fast-growing following.

name: Royal Docks CrossFit
who: East London box next to the ExCeL centre, one of the UK's most competition-focused CrossFit gyms.
why: A regular stop for touring elite athletes training in London, including Mat Fraser, Tia-Clair Toomey and Rich Froning.

name: CrossFit Reykjavik
who: Iceland's flagship box, training ground for the country's cluster of world-class CrossFit athletes.
why: Home of two-time Games champion Annie Thorisdottir and an international 'super team' of transplant athletes drawn to Iceland's training culture.

name: XT Oslo
who: One of the largest and oldest CrossFit facilities in Europe, spread across three training halls.
why: Anchors Oslo's functional-fitness scene, which also hosts the Oslo Throwdown, one of Northern Europe's biggest CrossFit competitions.

name: Cape CrossFit
who: South Africa's most competitive CrossFit team gym, a fixture of the Cape Town functional-fitness scene.
why: The winningest team in Fittest in Cape Town history and a Regionals qualifier every year since 2011.

name: Lvl Up CrossFit
who: CrossFit affiliate in Dubai's IMPZ district, part of the emirate's fast-growing functional-fitness box scene.
why: Represents Dubai's cluster of expat-driven CrossFit boxes that has grown alongside the city's fitness-tourism boom.

name: CrossFit Condesa
who: 800-square-meter box in central Mexico City, formerly branded Reebok CrossFit Plaza Condesa.
why: One of the largest and longest-running CrossFit facilities in Latin America's second-biggest CrossFit market.

name: Team Training UK
who: Official Hyrox training club in Cheshire, offering dedicated Hyrox race-prep programming alongside general fitness classes.
why: One of the UK's earliest gyms built specifically around Hyrox racing rather than retrofitted from a CrossFit box.

name: SKILL CGN
who: Official Hyrox performance-training gym in Cologne, one of Germany's hubs for the fast-growing race format.
why: Sits inside Hyrox's home market of Germany, which hosts some of the sport's largest annual events.

name: CrossFit Kailua
who: Community box on Oahu built around the Hawaiian concept of ohana (family), with a roster of CrossFit Games-level members.
why: One of the sport's early Games-era affiliates, still drawing fitness travelers to Hawaii's CrossFit scene.

name: Wasatch CrossFit
who: Davis County box coaching Salt Lake City-area athletes since 2007, one of Utah's first CrossFit affiliates.
why: 2017 CrossFit Games Affiliate Cup champions, a genuine national title that put a small-market gym on the map.

name: Second City CrossFit
who: One of Chicago's longest-running CrossFit boxes, a community fixture of the city's functional-fitness scene.
why: Represents the deep bench of veteran, non-flagship urban boxes that anchor CrossFit's everyday culture in major US cities.

name: Atlas Training Club
who: South Manchester and Cheshire's first gym built specifically for Hyrox training.
why: Illustrates Hyrox's rapid spread into purpose-built training clubs across the UK beyond London.
